outline.chapter_title: Foundations of Parameter-Efficient Finetuning and Orthogonal Constraints
outline.description: Introduce the motivation for parameter-efficient finetuning (PEFT) of large foundation models and the role of orthogonality in preserving pretrained knowledge. Establish notation and the learning setting assumed throughout the book.
subtopics: Why PEFT matters: cost, accessibility, and deployment constraints
PEFT families: model finetuning, adapter tuning, prompt/prefix tuning
Additive vs multiplicative reparameterizations
Preserving pretrained knowledge: small perturbations, relational structure, and angles between neurons
Orthogonality in ML: invariance of pairwise angles and stability
Notation and preliminaries for linear layers and transformers

outline.chapter_title: Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT): Principles, Parameterization, and Limitations
outline.description: Present the OFT framework, its mathematical formulation, and practical implementation, followed by a critical analysis of its parameter costs and inductive biases.
subtopics: OFT formulation: z = (R W0)^T x with R orthogonal
Cayley transform for orthogonal parameterization and skew-symmetric Q
Identity (zero) initialization and stability considerations
Block-diagonal OFT: structure, parameter counting, and inference cost
Benefits of OFT vs LoRA: preserving spectral properties and angles
Limitations: fixed sparsity pattern, reduced expressiveness, inability to approximate classic dense transforms

outline.chapter_title: An Information Transmission View of Orthogonal Matrix Factorization
outline.description: Recast dense orthogonal matrix construction as an information transmission problem on a grid graph, revealing design desiderata for sparse factorizations that achieve dense connectivity.
subtopics: Matrix multiplication unrolled as layered graphs
Nodes, edges, and nonzero entries: connectivity and information flow
Desiderata: dense connectivity and minimum free edges under orthogonality
Orthogonality-induced constraints between adjacent layers (bijective matchings)
Edge counting and examples: when composites are dense or not
Why block-diagonal OFT cannot yield dense connectivity

outline.chapter_title: Butterfly Structures and Fast Linear Transforms as a Design Prior
outline.description: Introduce butterfly graphs from the Cooley–Tukey FFT and their use as efficient sparse factorizations that enable global information exchange with logarithmic depth.
subtopics: Review of Cooley–Tukey FFT and butterfly networks
Butterfly factor B^F(k): definition and structure
Recursive butterfly matrix B(d) and its layered composition
Block butterfly components: tilde B^b(d, k) and permutations
Orthogonality of butterfly components via 2x2 (or 2b x 2b) orthogonal blocks
Complexity analysis: parameters and multiplies in O(d log d)

outline.chapter_title: Orthogonal Butterfly Finetuning (BOFT): Method and Parameterization
outline.description: Define BOFT as a generalized orthogonal finetuning framework that composes a dense orthogonal transform from a product of sparse orthogonal butterfly components, and detail its practical training recipe.
subtopics: BOFT forward pass: R(m, b) = product of orthogonal butterfly components
BOFT(m, b) family and special cases: BOFT(1, b)=block OFT; BOFT(1, d)=full OFT; BOFT(log d, 2)=dense butterfly
Parameter count and expressivity vs budget trade-offs
Identity initialization for stability and compatibility with pretrained models
Multiplicative dropout: block-wise identity replacement strategy
Implementation in transformers, vision backbones, and diffusion U-Nets
Choosing m and b under parameter budgets and latency constraints

outline.chapter_title: Theory and Properties: Expressivity, Spectral Behavior, and Inductive Bias
outline.description: Analyze BOFT’s representational power relative to OFT, its spectral stability, and the inductive biases introduced by butterfly structures, including connections to metric learning.
subtopics: Approximation of random orthogonal matrices and parameter-efficiency trends
Theorem: BOFT is more expressive than OFT with the same block size
Kaleidoscope hierarchy and conditions for spanning the orthogonal group
Spectral norm preservation and implications for stability and generalization
Bilinear similarity perspective: learning R in w_i^0 R x
Structured inductive bias: recovering classic transforms (FFT, DCT, Hadamard)

outline.chapter_title: Practical Usage and Empirical Evaluation Across Modalities
outline.description: Summarize empirical results of BOFT on large language models, vision transformers, and text-to-image diffusion models, and provide guidance for practitioners.
subtopics: Experimental setup: datasets, tasks, and evaluation metrics
Baselines: LoRA and OFT variants; adapter and prompt methods where relevant
Main results: accuracy, perplexity, FID, and other task metrics vs parameter count
Ablations: impact of m, b, component depth, and block size
Effect of multiplicative dropout and identity initialization
Training stability, convergence behavior, and weight interpolation observations
Runtime analysis: training overhead and zero-latency inference after folding

outline.description: Reflect on when to use BOFT, current limitations, and promising research directions enabled by the information transmission framework.
subtopics: When BOFT is preferable to LoRA or OFT and hybrid strategies
Limitations: training-time overhead and choice of topology
Beyond butterfly: alternative sparse factorizations inspired by network topologies
Combining low-rank and sparse structures; compatibility with quantization and pruning
Scalability, hardware-aware design, and deployment considerations
Open questions and suggested projects for further study
